bull_bear.body: CRAR 20.71% (from 22.4%) — dip partly from CLM shrinkage onto balance sheet. Strategy: conserve capital by routing incremental AUM through CLM/DA partners (de-lever from 4.89x). ~Rs 51 cr deeper-bucket NPA write-offs per board policy. True North (long-standing PE holder) fully exited 6.86% (25.7M shares) via block deal → acquired by **Nomura India Equity Fund** (FPI) — a shareholder-register change, not company capital.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: 1) **Gold regime optics** — reported 1+/30+ DPD and Stage 2 (2.2→2.7%) elevated as bullet→periodic-interest transitions; management says optical/auction-backed, not asset risk. 2) **Gold price** — 15% fall Jan-Jun; further falls compress LTV/AUM growth. 3) **Leverage at 4.89x** until CLM normalizes. 4) **LAP yield competition** (medium-ticket) — disbursal held for quality. 5) **Monsoon / West-Asia macro** — no stress seen yet, possible Q2-Q3. 6) **Mortgage Stage-3** — lengthy SARFAESI enforcement; collections team beefed up, "long haul".
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Parvez Mulla measured and consistent — "same set of priorities for five quarters, unchanged": secured book, gold+LAP twin engines, DA reduction, sub-1% credit cost. Candid that disbursal is deliberately an "outcome" (yield/quality first), that gold overdues will look optically worse, and that branch openings slipped to Q2. CFO C.V. Ganesh precise on DA accounting, FVOCI reclassification and the write-off math. Reiterated all FY27 guidances "intact." Tone: rebuild-credibility, under-promise/over-deliver.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The 52% PAT growth is core-income, not DA** — FEDFINA is deliberately shrinking DA income (negative Rs 13 cr) and still grew net income 33% and PPOP 50%; the DA wind-down is a self-inflicted headwind that makes the core trajectory cleaner going forward.
- **The gold regime change is a reported-delinquency reset, not a credit event** — entire bullet book moved to interest-due; a single missed interest now reports the whole loan overdue, so 1+/30+/Stage-2 optics rise sector-wide with unchanged auction economics.
- **Leverage spike (4.6→4.89x) is a CLM plumbing issue** — would-be co-lending sat on own balance sheet during the transition; de-leverage as partners re-onboard is a coming ROE tailwind.
- **Branch unification (gold + ST-LAP) is the quiet operating-leverage lever** — 400-500 gold branches with no ST-LAP = latent cross-sell on shared distribution/target-market.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- CRAR of 20.7% in Q1 FY27, down 169 bps both YoY and QoQ from 22.4%, as the balance sheet levered up — average total assets to average shareholders' fund rose to 5.9x from 5.1x a year earlier.
- Shareholder's Fund ₹3,003 Cr and Book Value Per Share ₹80.1 at Q1 FY27; borrowings ₹14,696 Cr against total assets of ₹18,247 Cr.
- Funding is deliberately multi-source: Term Loans 40%, Direct Assignments 14%, Net Worth 14%, ECB 12%, CPs 8%, CLM 7%, NCDs 5%.
- ALM as on 30 June 2026 is shown as cumulative surplus across every bucket, including a surplus of ₹1,603 Cr in the <3 months bucket and ₹7,338 Cr in the >5 year bucket.
- No dividend or buyback policy is disclosed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Gold Loans:** AUM Rs 11,191 cr (+77% YoY, 51.4% of book); LTV 67.9% (up from 61% on gold-price fall, on-boarding LTV unchanged); tonnage +1% QoQ (+8.1% QoQ AUM despite ~15% domestic gold price fall Jan-Jun + Apr-1 regime change). Lends on lower of 30-day avg or spot. Doorstep Gold Rs 1,787 cr (+96.5%). IGL (income-generating) product to compete with banks on higher-LTV.
- **Mortgages:** AUM Rs 9,777 cr (+14%); Medium-ticket LAP (Rs 35 lakh-3 cr, yield ~12-12.5%, Tier 1/2, competitive yield pressure) + Small-ticket LAP (Rs 7-35 lakh, yield ~16%, Tier 3/4). Disbursals held back on yield/approval-rate discipline ("growth is an outcome"). Old ST-LAP book behaving as guided; new book better delinquencies.
- **Co-lending (CLM) / DA:** transition issues under new gold rules pushed CLM onto own book (leverage 4.89x); Rs 589 cr LAP + ~Rs 300 cr gold DA done; DA income deliberately negative (unwinding > new booking).
- **Leadership:** George Oommen joins as Business Head – Gold Loans (30+ yrs, under Jagadeesh Rao); Shardul Kadam → Chief Transformation Officer; Jagadeesh Rao takes additional charge of ST LAP + Home Loans (branch as the "epicentre").

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Self-described as an 'MSME lender with focused loan against property and gold loans offering', with the vision 'Empowering Emerging India with Easy Access to Loans' and the tagline 'Focused entirely on collateralized lending'.
- Parentage is a stated moat: majority-owned by Federal Bank (60.7%) 'with strong access to debt & equity'; credit rating of AA+/Stable from all top four agencies (CARE, CRISIL, ICRA, India Ratings) plus Short Term A1+.
- Collateral quality is the positioning anchor: 99.2% of AUM is secured by either customer property or gold, 81.8% of mortgage AUM is secured by self-occupied residential/commercial property, and ~78% of mortgage AUM carries CIBIL >700.
- Addressable-market framing rests on third-party data: an INR 92 Tn MSME credit gap (INR 25 Tn within the formal sector) and household gold that is 93% unpledged versus 7% pledged with financiers, alongside household credit-to-GDP rising 34% (FY21) to 76% (FY28P).
- Growth journey narrative: AUM from ₹10 bn/107 branches/579 employees in FY17 to ₹211 bn/757 branches/5,376 employees in Q1 FY27, with milestones including True North joining as strategic partner and a ₹10.9 Bn IPO.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Regulation] The RBI Gold Loan Framework introduces exposure-based maximum LTV inclusive of principal plus interest (85% up to ₹2.5 Lakh, 80% for ₹2.5-5 Lakh, 75% above ₹5 Lakh), mandatory repayment-capacity assessment above ₹2.5 Lakh, fresh assessment on renewals/top-ups, and renewal only on Standard Assets.
- [Regulation - co-lending] The framework requires a minimum 10% exposure retained by each lender, exposure transfer to the partner within 15 days of disbursement, and caps Default Loss Guarantee at ≤5%; the deck warns that 'System and process alignment with the new guidelines across co-lending partners may temporarily moderate co-lending off-take'.
- [Shareholding] Nomura India Investment holds 6.9% following its acquisition of the stake from True North; other institutional holders include Bandhan Mutual Fund 3.2%, Unifi Capital 2.1% and SBI Life Insurance 1.9%.
- [Provisioning] Stage 2 ECL provision cover rose to 16.53% of Stage 2 assets in Q1 FY27 from 13.27% in Q1 FY26, and Stage 3 cover to 38.36% from 38.27% (32.29% in Q4 FY26); by product, Q1 FY27 PCR is 36.4% on mortgage, 21.3% on gold and 95.5% on business loans.
- [Asset quality by product] Mortgage carries materially higher stress than gold — Gross Stage III of 3.4% on mortgage versus 0.1% on gold and 25.2% on business loans in Q1 FY27.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Yield (ex-DA) +10 bps QoQ to 15.7% despite tanked-up liquidity (Gulf-geopolitics hedge) that kept incremental borrowing costs +20-30 bps over Q4; weighted-average CoB still fell 3 bps QoQ. Rate outlook benign on FCNRB flows in Q2. Cost-to-income improved >400 bps QoQ to 52.8% — primarily core-income expansion, aided by Q1 seasonally-low sourcing (expected to rise as originations pick up). Opex/avg total assets 4.8% (-70 bps), creating room to invest in 200 new branches while sustaining ROA. LAP yield under competitive pressure (~12-12.5% medium-ticket); FEDFINA holding yields rather than chasing disbursal.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** AUM Rs 21,136 cr (+35% YoY; gold Rs 11,191 cr +77%, mortgage Rs 9,777 cr +14%). PAT Rs 114.4 cr (+52.5%), ROE 15.4% (+380 bps), ROA 2.6%, EPS >Rs 3. GNPA 1.6% (-30 bps, ~Rs 51 cr write-off; normative 1.87%), NNPA <1.0%, PCR 38.36%, credit cost 0.8%. Yield ex-DA 15.7% (+10 bps), CoB -3 bps, C-I 52.8% (from 57.2%), opex/assets 4.8%, CRAR 20.71%, leverage 4.89x. Negative DA Rs 13 cr; Stage 2 2.2→2.7% (gold regime). True North exited 6.86% → Nomura India Equity Fund. Guidance intact: gold AUM +25-30% (flat price), entity +20-22%, mortgage/LAP +15-20%, credit cost <1%, ROA +20-30 bps, 200 branches, tonnage +10-12%, de-lever over coming quarters.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (1) do gold 1+/30+/Stage-2 optics stabilize under periodic-interest? (2) leverage de-levering from 4.89x as CLM normalizes; (3) 200-branch openings landing (Q2 spillover); (4) gold tonnage picking up H2; (5) LAP yield vs disbursal trade-off; (6) credit cost holding sub-1%; (7) FCNRB-led CoB relief._

deepdive.thesis: the near-term noise is optical, reported gold-loan overdues will look elevated as customers transition from bullet to periodic-interest structures, but this is "customer behaviour in transition, not an asset-quality concern" given highly realizable collateral.

open.item: Gold-loan AUM growth (on flat gold price)

Management is executing the revised gold LTV regime effective April 2026 (85% up to INR2.5 lakh, 80% up to INR5 lakh, 75% above); ~90% of book is under 75% LTV, margin breach won't impact NPA recognition.
Management expects gold yields to recover by Q1FY27 toward Q2FY26 levels if competition stays benign; LAP yields (MT and ST) expected to hold with only ~10 bps variation.

Management flagged hardening cost of borrowing post-February and rising FX hedge rates amid Gulf geopolitical uncertainty; tanked up on liquidity as a Q1 hedge, declining to guide incremental cost of funds.
Management is confident ST LAP will grow and turn accretive in FY27 as the new collection/leadership infrastructure gains vintage; Q4 disbursals INR289 cr (+39% QoQ), FY26 total INR904 cr.
Management expects fee/other income to pick up with LAP disbursal recovery, targeting 0.8% to 1% coming from the fee-income side on the ROA tree.
Management guided that even with flattish gold prices, gold AUM should grow 20-22% in FY27 on the back of 10-15% budgeted tonnage growth.
Management guided approximately 20-30 bps ROA improvement in FY27 over the FY26 average ROA (~2.4-2.5%), sourced from opex and credit-cost gains (~40 bps at PBT level).
Management guided overall AUM growth of 20-25% for FY27, reiterating the 20-25% AUM-growth-company framing.
Management maintains status quo on the RBI bank-owned-NBFC guidelines, awaiting the regulator's response to representations from FEDFINA and its parent given its listed-entity status.
Management stated Medium Ticket LAP will remain in the range of 20% to 25% of AUM as a stable, healthy book.

verdicts.item: Management guided to grow AUM at 25% year-on-year on a sustained basis, treating episodic gold-driven upside as opportunistic.
verdicts.note: 'On the AUM front, we have grown 27%, with our AUM touching 20,000 Cr... When excluding BL, we have observed an increase in AUM of 41%'; sustained growth above 25%.

verdicts.item: Management expects FY26 credit cost to stay around 1% plus or minus 10 bps, with flows expected in the next two quarters before normalizing by year-end.
verdicts.note: 'Our credit cost for Q4 stands at 0.7% and for FY26, it stands at 0.8%'; kept within/better than the 1% +/- 10 bps guide. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management targets raising doorstep gold loan share from ~15% of gold AUM to about 18-22% over the next one to two years.
verdicts.note: 'Doorstep gold loan stands at around INR1,730 crores AUM, which is 17% on the overall AUM'; just below the 18-22% target with a strong +108% trajectory. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Senior leadership placed in collections, structure verticalized by product; middle and field-level hiring in progress with substantial completion expected by Q1FY26.
verdicts.note: 'Collections, senior leadership has been onboarded, field team has been strengthened, the collection framework has been verticalized... almost 2x the collection personnel that we started with.'

verdicts.item: Management expects credit-cost normalization to set in by year-end (FY26) after flows plateau over the next two quarters.
verdicts.note: 'we have limited our credit cost for the year at 0.8% and for Q4 at 0.7%'; entity 1+ DPD improved to 6% from 7.1%; normalization delivered by year-end.

verdicts.item: Management plans to co-locate/source gold and ST LAP business from the same branches next year to improve cost efficiency.
verdicts.note: 'we have successfully further merged additional 7 branches, taking the total to 70 branches this year.'

verdicts.item: Management guided a possible 5 to 10 basis points improvement in cost to average total assets, while cost-to-income stays roughly flat given growth investments (rebuild year).
verdicts.note: 'On a full year basis, FY26 has seen a 20 bps drop in opex to average total assets over FY25'; beat the 5-10 bps improvement guide. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management reiterated FY26 credit cost will remain range-bound at 1% plus or minus 10 bps, absorbing residual BL and ST LAP flows.
verdicts.note: 'for FY26, it stands at 0.8%'; residual BL and ST LAP flows absorbed within/better than the 1% +/- 10 bps guide. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management plans to open gold loan branches in over 100 (guided 100-150) new markets in FY26, with substantial openings from Q2 onwards.
verdicts.note: 'we have opened 34 new gold branches this quarter, bringing our total to 148 new branches this year'; within the guided 100-150 range.

verdicts.item: Management (Jagadeesh) guided 25% year-on-year gold AUM growth with existing branches, plus delta from new branches.
verdicts.note: 'Gold reached INR10,352 crores, an AUM growth of 76%, substantiated by a tonnage growth of 12%'; well above the 25%+ guide.

verdicts.item: Management expects gold to remain in the 45-49% range of the mix (including 15-18% CLM), with mortgages covering the balance.
verdicts.note: Gold Rs.10,352 cr on Rs.20,153 cr entity AUM (~51%); exceeded the 45-49% band on unconstrained gold growth (management confirms no 50% cap). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: ST LAP transitioned to system-driven BRE/API workflows; credit scorecards and risk models targeted for rollout by Q3FY26, with a similar pilot planned for MT LAP.
verdicts.note: 'shift towards a system-driven BRE... We are seeing improvements in sourcing quality this year'; the Q3FY26 scorecard rollout and MT LAP pilot are not explicitly confirmed complete.
